#1332. The seven Anthropic founders who are about to become multi-billionaires

The seven Anthropic founders who are about to become multi-billionaires

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (895 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In the space of just five years, Anthropic has gone from unknown start-up to tech giant, worth more than a trillion dollars.
  • The firm behind the AI platform Claude was formed by seven people who left rival OpenAI in 2021 and, in a matter of hours, will become multi-billionaires - on paper at least.
  • Anthropic is floating the business on the US stock exchange and will sell its shares at between $70 - $78 each.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Brother and sister Dario and Daniela Amodei.

In the space of just five years, Anthropic has gone from unknown start-up to tech giant, worth more than a trillion dollars.

The firm behind the AI platform Claude was formed by seven people who left rival OpenAI in 2021 and, in a matter of hours, will become multi-billionaires - on paper at least.

Anthropic is floating the business on the US stock exchange and will sell its shares at between $70 - $78 each.

If they go for the highest price, the founders' shareholdings will be worth at least $18.5bn each.

So, who are these people, all in their thirties and forties, who are about to become incredibly wealthy?

In 2020, Dario Amodei was working for OpenAI, the firm that brought generative artificial intelligence to a mainstream audience, when it released Chat-GPT.

He decided he wanted to do things his own way, and left, taking his sister Daniela, and five colleagues with him.

Amodei grew up in San Francisco, impressing school friends not just with his academic prowess but also his speed on the running track, and his preoccupation with philosophical and technological questions including the potential of machines to gain consciousness and human longevity.

In a recent development, initially he studied physics at Princeton and Stanford. But following his father's death from hepatitis C, he switched to biology and biomedical sciences.

Amodei did stints at the Chinese tech giant Baidu and Google before joining OpenAI.

But he began to worry that some people within the manufacturer were putting profit before safety, prompting the decision to jump ship.

Now 43, he is Anthropic's chief executive, and the person who, in his sister's words, makes the manufacturer "ambitious".

Listen: Dario Amodei BBC Sounds profile.

Sources indicate that dario and Daniela Amodei, were close growing up and later shared a flat together in San Francisco with other friends. She followed him into OpenAI and joined him when he left to found Anthropic.

She and her brother have always genuinely liked each other, she says, but the only thing she ever did first, was when he followed her in becoming vegetarian.

Amodei studied English Literature at the University of California Santa Cruz, going on to work for Democrat representative Matt Cartwright.

She has also worked at financial services platform Stripe, where she was head of risk operations.

The 39-year-old is president of Anthropic, manages the executive team, and leads the firm's research, engineering, product, governance and commercial work.

Tom Brown, now 39, followed the Amodei siblings when they left to found their latest venture.

He led GPT-3 engineering at OpenAI, and prior to that was at Google on its DeepMind project.

Brown established his entrepreneurial credentials co-founding an app called "Grouper" that helps set up drinks between groups of friends.

He has supported US President Donald Trump's stance on datacentres, arguing that they are "an enormous source of prosperity".

Now as chief compute officer at Anthropic he is responsible for how the firm secures and uses its computing resources.

Jack Clark, is another arts graduate among the original start-up's founding members and the only one who is not from North America.

Originally from Brighton in the UK, he studied English Literature and Creative Writing at the University of East Anglia and became a technology journalist, writing for publications including ZDNet UK, The Register, and Bloomberg.

He was caught up in the excitement of artificial intelligence and joined OpenAI, where he worked initially in communications, later becoming its policy director.

Now, 37, Clark is head of public benefit at Anthropic. He also leads the Anthropic Institute, an AI think tank.

Jared Kaplan, 42, is chief science officer at Anthropic, and heads its technical research. He is also an associate professor at Johns Hopkins University in Baltimore.

He holds a PhD in physics from Harvard University.

His work on scaling laws - which describe mathematical patterns that show that bigger AI models trained on more data tend to be more consistent - has helped provide AI firms with a framework for predicting AI behaviour, according to Anthropic.

Chris Olah is described as "interpretability research lead" primarily focused on how AI models work with each other.

But according to the Fresh York Times, Olah has spent much of the last year convening meetings with faith leaders from across the religious spectrum.

Described by the newspaper as "boyish" but with "the zeal of an evangelist" the 34-year-old is reportedly exploring the relationship between morality and AI.

He previously led interoperability research at OpenAI, and prior to that was a research scientist at Google Brain.

The Canadian left Toronto University early, but later secured a Thiel Fellowship of $100,000, which is a scholarship to help gifted people move into research without a degree.

It has been revealed that sam McCandlish, 36, takes less of a public-facing role than the other founders, but like them will own around 1.6% of the manufacturer after its shares go on sale. As a result he too will see his stake crystallise into a hugely valuable asset.

Sources indicate that mcCandlish is Anthropic's chief architect, and helps shape and implement the organization's policy designed to mitigate the risks of AI. Prior to this he worked on safety at OpenAI.

He has a physics PhD from Stanford, and maths and physics degree from Brandeis University outside Boston.

After being barebones at launch, Google is improving on Pixel 11 Pro’s Hilight feature with message support, now including WhatsApp.

As a part of the November 2026 Pixel Drop that was released this week, Google Messages added support for HiLight on the Pixel 11 Pro series. As we reported back in September when Google started beta testing the functionality, people can select a contact and enable a specific color light for phone calls and/or messages.

Recent findings suggest that am I that old, or does no one else remember when Blackberry had a colored light that could be configured to run a rainbow of different colors with different patterns for any app notification. What's old is latest again....

Google’s announcement only officially introduced support for the Google Messages app but, as it turns out, WhatsApp is also supported.

Shenaz Zack, Senior Director of Product Management over Pixel, confirmed through a brief video on Twitter/X that WhatsApp messages can also now activate HiLight. This isn’t a huge surprise given WhatsApp calls have been supported since day one, but it’s a nice addition for the many users who prefer WhatsApp over SMS/RCS.

HiLight already worked with WhatsApp calls and now, it works with WhatsApp messages, too, doing the heavy lifting so my favorites get the VIP attention 😄 pic.twitter.com/ouLROk1FeF.

Android 17 QPR2 enables the update, and it’s rolling out now to all Pixel 11 Pro devices.

CFTC and Justice Department sue Arkansas and Louisiana over event-contract crackdowns

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (635 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Readwrite

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In two days, federal authorities filed suits against two states that treat prediction markets as illegal gambling.
  • The federal government has opened two new court fights with states over prediction markets.
  • It has been revealed that the Arkansas complaint carries case number 4:26-cv-01255-BSM.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In two days, federal authorities filed suits against two states that treat prediction markets as illegal gambling. The cases could decide whether state gaming regulators or the CFTC control sports event contracts, which compete with licensed sportsbooks and online casinos.

The federal government has opened two new court fights with states over prediction markets. Both target state actions against event contracts offered on CFTC-regulated exchanges. Arkansas and Louisiana treat those contracts as illegal gambling. Washington argues that federal law takes priority.

It has been revealed that the Arkansas complaint carries case number 4:26-cv-01255-BSM. It is aimed at the enforcement action Griffin filed against KalshiEX LLC and Kalshi Inc. That state suit alleges multiple violations of the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act. It seeks restitution, penalties, taxes and injunctive relief.

In release 9325-26, the CFTC noted Arkansas could seek civil penalties against CFTC-registered exchanges that could reach hundreds of millions of dollars. The federal suit also aims to stop the state from halting event-contract trading. The government wants a preliminary and permanent injunction. That order would bar Arkansas officials from investigating CFTC-regulated entities, their affiliates and partners. It would also stop them from enforcing state law against those firms over transactions on designated contract markets.

It has been revealed that griffin’s stance is not latest. In October 2025, he issued a formal opinion that sports event contracts are gambling and require a license. The new case brings the preemption fight into the Eighth Circuit, which has not yet ruled on the question.

Recent findings suggest that with Arkansas added, the CFTC’s tally of state lawsuits over federal authority reaches 11. The agency has also filed amicus briefs in four federal appeals courts and one state supreme court.

Sources indicate that the Louisiana case moved within a day. Judge Jeffrey Johnson of the 21st Judicial District Court in Tangipahoa Parish signed the restraining order. The named entities are linked to Kalshi, Polymarket, Robinhood, Crypto.com, Coinbase, Gemini, ForecastEx, Novig, Underdog, IG Group and ProphetX.

Sources indicate that in release 9326-26, the CFTC noted the order shut down more than 30 companies tied to CFTC-regulated derivatives without giving them notice or a chance to be heard. The federal suit was filed in the Eastern District of Louisiana. It names the state, Attorney General Liz Murrill, the Louisiana Gaming Control Board and the state police gaming enforcement division. It asks the court to declare state gambling laws preempted. It also seeks to stop Louisiana from enforcing or extending the state order.

🚨Breaking: Louisiana judge orders temporary restraining order prohibiting Kalshi, Polymarket, Coinbase, Robinhood, and other “prediction market” operators from continuing their unlicensed and unregulated illegal gambling in Louisiana.

It’s not complicated: if you aren’t a… pic.twitter.com/gzrQlN9CCL.

— Attorney General Liz Murrill (@AGLizMurrill) November 12, 2026.

In a recent development, the exchange between officials has been sharp. CFTC Chairman Michael Selig described Louisiana’s emergency suit as “naked lawfare and a cynical political stunt.” On Nov. 14, Murrill answered on X. She accused Selig of “flatly false statements” and argued that states have regulated gambling for 250 years.

In a recent development, for licensed sportsbooks and online casinos, the outcome matters directly. If federal preemption holds, sports event contracts could operate outside state gaming rules in both states. The federal requests to block both states’ actions now go before the U.S. District Courts for the Eastern Districts of Arkansas and Louisiana.

#1329. Grand Theft Auto VI has arrived

Grand Theft Auto VI has arrived

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (963 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: The Verge

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that more than a decade after Grand Theft Auto V was first released, its sequel is finally launching.
  • Part of this has to do with the success of its predecessor, as GTA V sold more than 230 million copies over the last 13 years.
  • According to recent reports, but GTA VI is now a real thing you can play, and you can also keep track of all of the notable post-launch information right here.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that more than a decade after Grand Theft Auto V was first released, its sequel is finally launching. On November 19th, GTA VI will be available on both the PS5 and Xbox Series X / S, and it’s quite possibly the most anticipated video game launch of all time.

Part of this has to do with the success of its predecessor, as GTA V sold more than 230 million copies over the last 13 years. Some of it has to do with the sheer length of time between releases, a period that was plagued by leaks and a handful of delays that made the wait even harder for fans.

According to recent reports, but GTA VI is now a real thing you can play, and you can also keep track of all of the notable post-launch information right here. That includes our own review and interviews with the development team, as well as news on just how the game ends up resonating with players.

Recent findings suggest that it took 13 years, a reported 10-figure budget, and the weight of the world’s expectations, but Grand Theft Auto VI is here. And it’s fantastic. The Verge’s Andrew Webster takes a break from the game to tell us all about life in Vice City, and why GTA VI’s approach to coffee tells us everything we need to know.

It has been revealed that lost in the excitement of GTA VI finally launching is the fact that Rockstar employees are in the process of voting on whether or not to unionize. Developer Nestor Uriarte explains the importance of the moment in an essay in The Guardian:.

Winning union recognition would be a huge step forward in securing a meaningful say over our conditions at Rockstar, but its significance would reach far beyond that. As one of the biggest and most influential game studios in the world, what happens here could open the door for other workers across the UK to imagine an alternative future for the industry – one in which workers’ voices are taken into account more.

According to recent reports, now that reviews have dropped for the game, it has skyrocketed to the top of Metacritic’s highest-rated list, surpassing Ocarina of Time (the original, not the remake). Of course, this could change as more reviews trickle in, but for now it’s safe to say that GTA VI was worth the long wait.

Grand Theft Auto VI isn’t just the biggest GTA game to date; it’s also the most romantic. Though the series is well known for its sordid assortment of criminal leads, GTA VI switches things up by starring a pair of thieves who also happen to fall in love after meeting while stealing a car. It’s still an open-world action game full of chaos and mayhem. But many players will also be attempting to nurture the budding relationship in between heists. The sprawling game is designed to support both audiences.

Sources indicate that “It’s a risk,” explains Rob Nelson, producer on GTA VI and co-studio head at developer Rockstar North. “It’s a real change for Grand Theft Auto. You can still play it the old way, you can reject all of this stuff. But for people who do engage, it’s meaningful — you’re earning it, you’re working at it, just like in a normal relationship.”.

How do you follow a game like Grand Theft Auto V? Thirteen years ago, Rockstar’s crime-fueled epic went on to redefine what an open-world game could be and became an enormous success, selling more than 230 million copies across three generations of game consoles. It sits just behind Tetris and Minecraft on the list of the best-selling games of all time, and its lucrative online mode has helped it remain popular for well over a decade.

That level of success has allowed Rockstar to take its time with a sequel, which has further increased the hype around the next GTA. A series of major leaks and delays only exacerbated this. At a time when much of the video game industry is struggling, the next edition of GTA stands alone, a cultural moment so big (almost) everybody has been forced to get out of the way. The buildup to Grand Theft Auto VI’s launch is unlike anything the game industry has ever seen.

Sony has confirmed the 1.267GB download is mandatory to play the new Grand Theft Auto when it launches at midnight tonight. As with most PlayStation firmware patches, we don’t know what it does though, beyond “some security fixes to the system software.”.

Rockstar hasn’t publicly said who is playing the two leads in GTA VI, but The Game Awards’ nominee video indicates that Manni L. Perez has been nominated for Best Performance for her work in the game.

GTA VI earned eight nominations, the most of any title, including one for Game of the Year.

Arion Kurtaj, a member of the Lapsus$ cybercrime group who leaked 90 videos of Grand Theft Auto VI in 2022 and hacked other significant companies, pleaded guilty on Monday, according to the UK’s Crown Prosecution Service (CPS).

Kurtaj, who is now 21, hacked BT/EE sometime between August and November 2021, and starting in early November of that year, the organization “noted a marked increase in unauthorised SIM swaps of their customers mobile phones.” He was charged for those offenses and moved to a hotel for his “own protection” in September 2022, but “breached his bail conditions to carry out further hacks on major companies using a mobile phone, the hotel TV’s Wi-Fi and a firestick,” including hacks on Rockstar Games, Uber, and Revolut, the CPS claims.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A set of major tech outages in close succession is leading some to speculate that they are connected, and that the US is under systemic attack by a hostile state.

All the evidence suggests otherwise, with individual explanations for each of them – and the White House is now saying as much in a bid to put fears to rest ….

It has been revealed that on Thursday, a widespread Microsoft 365 outage ran into the following day when two unrelated challenges coincided. Friday saw a nationwide ground stop of US air traffic due to a communication concern affecting all air traffic control centers. On Monday, a bug in a Chase bank system saw disruption not only to the bank itself, but also other banks where Chase was a party to a transaction. Finally, yesterday saw many Apple services offline, with retail stores also affected.

The Apple outage doesn’t appear to have been significant enough to have reached the administration’s radar, but CBS News reports secretary of state Marco Rubio saying the others are unrelated.

Sources indicate that “The Microsoft incident has nothing to do with what we saw with the FAA. The FAA has nothing to do with what we saw with the banks a few days ago. These problems that we’ve seen from a technical standpoint are completely unrelated one from another,” Rubio said […].

“We have zero evidence or any reason to believe that any of these isolated or individual instances have anything to do with nefarious actors, with cyber hackers, with criminals, with another nation state, with a malign actor of any kind. Each of them are distinct, and they’re different in their causation.”.

The statement was backed by Senator Mark Warner.

Democratic Sen. Mark Warner, vice chair of the Senate Intelligence Committee, also said on Tuesday that there’s no indication these incidents are the result of an attack.

Warner went on to say that the ability of AI systems to find vulnerabilities at “unprecedented speed” does, however, mean companies and government agencies alike need to be ready to patch vulnerabilities immediately.

Grand Theft Auto VI is officially out and critics love it.

Recent findings suggest that unleashed on Wednesday 13 years after its predecessor, Rockstar Games' wildly anticipated game has landed the highest ever rating on Metacritic. Essentially, it's instantly the best-reviewed game of all time, according to the aggregator site.

According to recent reports, GTA 6 has a 99 percent rating on Metacritic, based on 147 critic reviews. This is a weighted average of individual critic scores calculated by Metacritic staff through a complex system involving review detail, publication prestige, and whether the critic has provided a score in their review.

Metacritic predicted GTA 6 would average 96 percent, an already staggering number it's blown out of the water.

In a dramatic twist, GTA 6 also accelerated past the previous #1 ranked game of all time, 1998 classic The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which has just dominated headlines with Nintendo's new remastered version.

Critics have dubbed GTA 6 everything from "the single most impressive video game I have ever played" to "a masterpiece of open-world design." Meanwhile, players are spending their first few hours with the game and reacting in real-time.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a lab near Newark Airport in New Jersey, a team of around 30 experienced human sniffers are slowly working their way through every odor on Earth. Their careful notes—“nutty,” “peachy,” “marine”—are cross-referenced with a chemical analysis to create a rich set of training data for what AI startup Osmo calls the world’s first foundation model for smell. The manufacturer’s goal, indicates founder Alex Wiltschko, is “to give computers a sense of smell.”.

Recent findings suggest that “Scent molecules are really the only language most species on this planet can speak,” he says. “Most species can’t communicate with sound or visually, so it truly is Earth’s original language. And it’s incredibly powerful for us, from a memory and an emotional standpoint. You can smell something once and remember it for the rest of your life. You can smell something on the street and be pulled back to high school.”.

Recent findings suggest that in the last few months, Wiltschko claims, Osmo’s model has achieved “human-level olfactory intelligence.” The organization’s definition of this is that the model is about as good as the average person at detecting and discriminating between smells, and about as good as a junior perfume designer at creating them. It says its technology is already being used in the fragrance industry to help brands design and manufacture fresh scents. Last month, the company says, Osmo’s AI model outperformed in-house perfumers at one of the world’s largest consumer goods companies. Wiltschko believes it could be deployed eventually for threat detection at airports, for example, or diagnosing diseases.

Industry observers note that wiltschko spun the startup out of his work at Google Brain, the search giant’s former AI research lab, in 2023, and he is running the same playbook as AI startups in other domains: Throw a lot of data at difficult problems, and see what happens. The challenge with scent, Wiltschko says, is that there was a dearth of good data. Before Osmo, there were fewer than 200,000 human descriptions of smells in existing databases, by his count. Plus, the chemical sensor devices needed to collect data are expensive, and the fragrance industry is secretive about its work on olfactory science.

Sources indicate that A lot of the company’s work has been in creating its own dataset of more than 10 million human labels and 800 million “scent tokens,” which describe the exact molecules and concentrations that go into creating specific odors. Osmo uses spectrometers and other chemical sensors, running around the clock, to break down the molecular makeup of everything from fruit and flowers to pantry  staples and organs. A team of around 70 trained data labelers in the US and overseas spend their days sniffing things and writing down what they smell like, using a standardized fragrance vocabulary.

Mapping out scents in this way is throwing out some unlikely parallels. In the same way that changing the order of words can drastically influence the meaning of a sentence, rearranging scent molecules in different proportions can drastically alter the smells humans perceive. “The scent tokens that define the smell of a newborn baby have massive overlap with the scent tokens in a fresh plate of cooked spaghetti,” Wiltschko says. (Specifically Barilla brand spaghetti, he says, which perhaps raises some questions for the people at the pasta factory.).

The firm also creates its own scents, using a smell-printing robot the size of a school bus that mixes ingredients according to precise formulas to make samples for Osmo’s own research and fragrances for paying customers. It can design and print scents to order based on a ChatGPT-style prompt. Wiltschko flipped open his laptop to show me how the AI model worked. He opened a text box on screen, and I asked him to generate a fragrance that smelled like a Portuguese custard tart (we were in Lisbon for Web Summit), aimed at 18- to 23-year-old men. The system spent a few minutes cogitating, then generated three options for potential scent profiles that matched the brief (creamy, coconutty, fruity) and the molecules needed to create them. If I’d continued with the ordering process, my signature L’Eau de Custard would have been ready about a week later.

In a recent development, osmo’s technology has already been used to create retail fragrances, including for giants like Procter & Gamble. The Gates Foundation, which invested $5 million when Osmo introduced, later gave the firm a $3.5 million grant to assess molecules that repel disease-carrying insects, and Osmo identified eight substances that were more repellent than DEET. Osmo has also worked with StockX, the online clothing marketplace, on using smell to spot counterfeit sneakers by detecting differences in the chemical composition of the materials used in the shoes.

It has been revealed that but not everyone is convinced by the technology or the tech giant’s substantial claims. Avery Gilbert, a smell scientist and author of What the Nose Knows, has been sharply critical of Osmo on his Substack, arguing that some of its marketing claims are undocumented, and that its patent filings still rely on human sensory panels and perfumers, rather than AI. “This heavy reliance on human sensory judgments seems odd for a company premised on super-cool AI,” he wrote in March. A representative for Osmo did not respond in time for publication.

In a recent development, michael Schmuker, a former professor of neural computation at the University of Hertfordshire who has previously consulted for Osmo, says the organization’s technology is an achievement. With colleagues, he created an open-source, reverse-engineered version of Osmo’s 2023 model, but it lacks the reams of data the company has collected since.

According to recent reports, but even with all this smell data, Osmo may be missing some of the factors that make human olfaction unique, Schmuker says. “Smell is super complex. Context is very vital for smell. The same molecule may evoke a different association depending on context,” he says. “[The smell of] a French cheese like Camembert is partly the same molecule as in used nappies. You don’t confuse the two because of the context.”.

Recent findings suggest that in a controlled setting like a fragrance lab, this lack of context may not matter so much. But it could have an impact if Osmo’s technology becomes, as Wiltschko suggests, the “olfactive channel” for AI world models. Imagine a machine that could sniff out spoilage in food on a production line, or detect tumors through smell the way dogs have been trained to do in pilot studies.

In a recent development, for that to happen, sensor technology will need to get a lot better, Schmuker says. The models will need to keep improving. Medical diagnostics is the biggest prize.

Recent findings suggest that “There’s a lot of history of companies that have gone directly at that mountain peak and, unfortunately, not been successful, because it is very expensive and it is very difficult,” Wiltschko says. "So what we’re doing is building this foundation at the foothills of all these mountains. We’re sending expeditions up to the mountains, doing explorations, and basically smelling the whole world.”.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is a masterpiece, say critics

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Review scores for GTA 6 are a fairytale ending after years of development.
  • After 13 years of waiting, record-breaking trailers and lengthy delays, critics have given their answer to one of the year's biggest questions.
  • Does Grand Theft Auto 6, surely the most anticipated game of all time, live up to the hype?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Review scores for GTA 6 are a fairytale ending after years of development.

After 13 years of waiting, record-breaking trailers and lengthy delays, critics have given their answer to one of the year's biggest questions.

Does Grand Theft Auto 6, surely the most anticipated game of all time, live up to the hype?

According to the first reviews, it's a resounding yes.

Metacritic, which aggregates reviews from critics, averages it at 99 out of 100, external - tying with Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which has held the record since 1998.

Reviewers overwhelmingly agreed the open-world action game was an ambitious, ground-breaking title that was well worth the wait.

Not everyone is enjoying the glowing praise - with some posters to online forums objecting to what one called "the ultra fan-boy hype.".

But there is no question the reviewers have been effusive with their praise, with gaming website IGN, external branding GTA 6 "unprecedented", "unbelievable" and "unmissable".

Meanwhile in its five star review, Eurogamer stated makers Rockstar had "pushed back the horizon of video games once again" with its graphics, storytelling and world building.

"The awe is all part of the point, of course, and GTA 6 is nothing if not truly awesome," reviewer Chris Tapsell wrote, external, but he added "there are also nits to pick".

For The Fresh York Times, external one of those nits was whether the realism of the game might dull the fun chaos of its predecessors.

Reviewer Yussef Cole mentioned GTA 6 had "matured beyond its memorable car crashes and stickups" with consequences to every action.

But "some of my favourite moments have been careening through streets with squad cars in hot pursuit," he wrote.

Critics say the relationship between Jason and Lucia is central to the game.

The graphics of the game were hotly anticipated and so far have not disappointed critics, with The Guardian, external describing Leonida, the setting inspired by Miami, as "so lifelike that at times it beggars belief".

And the relationship between the lead characters, Jason and Lucia, has also stunned critics.

"They feel like real people rather than puppets dancing to your whim," The Guardian's Keza MacDonald wrote, adding: "I found it impossible not to care for them".

Writing for Forbes, external, Paul Tassi noted: "I can't say I've ever seen a better video game relationship than the one they share".

The Washington Post, external said GTA 6 "raises the bar at every level", while Bloomberg, external's Jason Schreier called it a "masterpiece" in his five star review.

Recent findings suggest that "It's hard not to be astonished by what Rockstar has done here," he wrote. "There's nothing else like it.

"While playing this game, I often found myself wondering how it even exists.".

Rockstar hasn't revealed the cost of the game, but some estimates put the figure north of $1bn (Â£760m).

GTA 6 is the most hotly anticipated videogame ever.

The Game Awards - the most watched ceremony of its kind in the industry - gave players a teaser of the critical reception when its 2026 nominations were revealed on Tuesday.

And despite having not released at the time, GTA 6 was the most-nominated title.

It will be up for eight prizes, including game of the year and best music.

The nomination of Manni L Perez in the best performance category confirmed wide speculation that she is the actress behind main character Lucia in GTA 6 - a fact Rockstar hadn't previously officially confirmed.

The jury for the event is largely made up of gaming journalists around the world, who would have received advanced copies for review.

Some, though, have questioned how a game that has just been released has garnered such positive reviews and award nominations.

There is a view in some online forums that the hype around the game has got out of control as, with one poster commenting: "I think everyone's tired of hearing about this game - I don't even want to play it anymore.".

It appears so far, however, that is likely to be very much a minority view.

Nubia Redmagic 12 Pro Review: Furiously Fast but Flawed

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1226 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mobile gamers don’t have many dedicated gaming smartphones to choose from, so Nubia’s Redmagic series stands out.
  • Industry observers note that sadly, Nubia has followed every other phone manufacturer this year, offering minimal iterative improvements while jacking up the price significantly.
  • Recent findings suggest that the Nubia Redmagic 12 Pro sports the same boxy design as its predecessors, just a teeny bit slimmer and lighter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mobile gamers don’t have many dedicated gaming smartphones to choose from, so Nubia’s Redmagic series stands out. This major, boxy phone offers cutting-edge performance, long battery life, and a large display. You also get touch-sensitive shoulder buttons, RGB lighting, and gaming-focused software features.

Industry observers note that sadly, Nubia has followed every other phone manufacturer this year, offering minimal iterative improvements while jacking up the price significantly. While this series has always been a clear bargain for gamers seeking the best chipset, it’s harder to swallow the compromises lurking here (camera, software, update commitment) when the price starts at $949.

Recent findings suggest that the Nubia Redmagic 12 Pro sports the same boxy design as its predecessors, just a teeny bit slimmer and lighter. I’m a fan of the translucent industrial aesthetic and RGB lighting, but it’s not something I really want in my everyday phone. I had exactly the same complications with the 12 Pro as I had with the 10 Pro I reviewed two years ago. It’s very massive, so you really feel it in your pocket, and it can be awkward to handle, especially when you’re trying to scroll one-handed. It’s also the most slippery phone ever. Every time I put it down, the 12 Pro slowly starts to slide away.

The big positive of this design is that it feels great in landscape orientation for gaming. The thick frame is easy to hold. There are touch-sensitive shoulder buttons on the top edge, and Nubia has a dedicated Magic Key for gaming mode, though you can customize it to launch the camera. This used to be a switch, but is now a red button. It’s still flanked by the round power button. Sadly, there’s no headphone port.

It’s refreshing not to have a camera bump on the back, though this inevitably adds to the slipperiness, and this glass sandwich swiftly gets covered in finger smudges. Nubia has toned down the lighting a little, but you can still customize it for all sorts of activities. There’s a powerful cooling fan inside, with two vents to expel hot air, but the 12 Pro still somehow scores an IP68/69 rating for dust and water resistance.

In a recent development, the 6.85-inch OLED display is completely uninterrupted, with no notch or cutout camera to break it up. There’s an effective fingerprint sensor at the bottom and a less effective selfie camera under the top of the screen. The screen can hit a 185-Hz refresh rate, but only a handful of games actually support it. Most of the time you’ll be capped at 120 Hz. It supports HDR with 5,000-nit local peak brightness for highlights, but overall brightness is capped at 1,900 nits. Overall, it’s a lovely display, and a pleasure to play games or watch movies on. The Dolby Atmos–certified stereo speakers are decent for a phone.

Perhaps the biggest enticement is Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chipset, paired with Redmagic’s RedCore R5 chipset and 12 or 16 GB of RAM. You won’t find a faster Android phone right now, and the Redmagic 12 Pro can even give the iPhone 18 Pro a run for its money. Benchmark scores topped the Android charts, above phones like Samsung’s Galaxy S26 Ultra.

In a recent development, I had no challenges playing Asphalt Legends and Wuthering Waves with settings cranked to the max. I also tried PUBG Mobile, one of the titles that can support that 185-Hz refresh rate, and it was smooth sailing. The 12 Pro keeps its cool, even after an hour or so of challenging gaming. Aside from the fan and vapor chamber for cooling, Nubia added dual-loop liquid cooling. You do get some fan noise and thermal throttling, but the 12 Pro has enough grunt to satisfy even the most hardcore of gamers.

To keep you gaming for longer, the 12 Pro boasts an enormous 8,400-mAh battery. Even with hours of gaming, I made it to the end of every day with something left in the tank. With careful use, you could easily push this phone to two days. There’s no charger in the box, but it supports up to 80-watt wired or wireless charging if you spring for a Redmagic charger. It took me an hour and 17 minutes to charge it from dead, but you can hit around 50 percent in half an hour. Sadly, it doesn’t support Qi2 magnets, so you’ll need a flat wireless charging pad.

To get top-notch performance at this price, you’ll have to accept several compromises. Let’s start with the camera. While the main 50-megapixel camera is quite good, and there’s a 50-megapixel ultrawide, the flat design doesn’t leave room for a telephoto lens, so you can only get 2X zoom by cropping. The main camera will satisfy folks who only snap the odd photo, and it does well in most conditions. The ultrawide is fine for group shots, but its smaller sensor means performance suffers in low light. The 16-megapixel front-facing camera is hidden under the screen, and it’s fine for video calls or well-lit selfies, though shots often look a bit muddy.

In a recent development, the real problem with the 12 Pro’s camera is the processing. Use the terrible portrait mode or zoom in too far and you’ll see how badly it handles image processing. Nubia lacks Google’s expertise in this space, so a camera system that sounds similar on paper produces far worse photos in reality. Nubia’s colors often look a bit off, it really struggles with mixed lighting, and shots tend to be noisy or oversharpened. Video recording is quite good with the main camera, but stabilization was a little poor in some of the videos I shot.

Recent findings suggest that another substantial turnoff with the 12 Pro is the software. Redmagic OS 12 sits atop Android 17, and it’s mostly OK, though I wish Chinese manufacturers didn’t feel the need to imitate things like Apple’s Liquid Glass. The interface also has some bad translations. What’s worse is the prevalence of absolute junk bloatware and the subpar enhancement commitment. Nubia is only promising two years of platform updates and three years of security software updates in the US (five years in the UK).

Recent findings suggest that our best Android phones guide includes many more well-rounded options than the 12 Pro. You can even buy a Pixel 11 Pro XL on sale for the same price right now. But the 12 Pro is all about gaming, and to that end, it offers the best performance-and-screen combo you can get today. Whether the gaming features, cooling tech, and overall style add enough value depends on you. That same chipset will roll into more phones soon, and most of them will have a better camera and longer software support, but they’re likely to be more expensive, like the forthcoming Motorola Signature 27 at $1,600.

It has been revealed that for buyers in the US, check your carrier bands. The 12 Pro should be fine with T-Mobile and its associated MVNOs, but it may not work well, or at all, with some other carriers. It also doesn’t support eSIM, so you need a physical SIM card. The 12-GB RAM and 256-GB storage model is $949; upgrading to 16 GB and 512 GB costs $1,049, and the 1-TB model is $1,199.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

First appearing earlier this month, Google Pixel phones are rolling out a handy fresh Family feature in the Settings menu. Here’s what it can do.

In a recent development, rolling out now via what appears to be a server-side update (tied to Google Play Services), Google Pixel phones are adding a “Family” section to the Settings menu. The feature is appearing for us on a Pixel 11 Pro XL running the October 2026 update (not Android 17 QPR2), while a Pixel 10 Pro has also just surfaced the newly introduced UI.

This fresh section, which Google has previously referred to as “Family Hub,” gives users a quick place to see their family members and settings in one central location. It shows a list of your family members – child accounts and anyone attached to your Google One family strategy – with controls over Google One storage, Google Play Family Library, shared payment methods, and “Family events” in Google Calendar.

Industry observers note that you can also see the live location of any family members you are sharing your location with or start sharing your location with another family member. You can also easily remove or add members to your family plan via this new menu. Each family member gets their own page where you can see benefits shared, location, and also if they are a “parent” in the family – with “remove” and “transfer” options available.

I've had it for a few weeks, and while it's surely something useful for those with a "family setup", it's IMHO a major annoyance for those who don't (who, I suspect, are the vast majority).

Couldn't they have it show up only for those "in a family"?

It's there, at the top, doing absolutely nothing useful for the vast majority of owners, and pushing down all other options.

While this won’t be helpful for all consumers, it’s certainly full of useful shortcuts and tools for those at the center of a family initiative and looking to share benefits with their household.

As far as we can tell, this is widely rolled out to Pixel owners at this point. As mentioned, we’re seeing it across multiple devices, and 9to5Google readers mentioned they’re also seeing it live even prior to installing the latest system revision. The folks at Droid-Life also mention now seeing it on their Pixels.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • When MacPaw launched Moonlock on the Mac, the company described its latest app as something that “complements Apple’s built-in security tools, protects from Mac-specific malware, and helps you understand cybersecurity better.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that after launching Moonlock for Mac last year, MacPaw is bringing its scam-detection app to iPhone today. Here are the details.

When MacPaw launched Moonlock on the Mac, the company described its latest app as something that “complements Apple’s built-in security tools, protects from Mac-specific malware, and helps you understand cybersecurity better.”.

In a recent development, in practice, the Mac app includes real-time protection against potential threats. Consumers can also manually scan their Mac for malware, including suspicious files hidden in system folders and email attachments.

Sources indicate that beyond that, Moonlock includes a VPN to encrypt internet traffic, a network inspector that demonstrates where apps are sending data and lets consumers block connections to specific countries, and an AI-powered scam detector that analyzes messages pasted into the app for signs of phishing. It also helps users review and adjust macOS security settings.

Today, MacPaw is launching Moonlock for iPhone, a move the company says “helps people recognize potential scams, understand their iPhone’s security and take practical steps to improve it.”.

Unlike the Mac version, Moonlock for iPhone doesn’t scan for malware, as iOS prevents third-party apps from accessing other apps and their files. Instead, it focuses on identifying potential scams, checking for exposed personal information, and helping users improve their iPhone’s security.

On the iPhone, Moonlock lets users rapidly check suspicious texts, screenshots, and QR codes for phishing, in addition to checking whether their email addresses have appeared in known data breaches.

According to recent reports, as MacPaw explains it, Moonlock’s Scam Detect “helps people check suspicious messages they encounter throughout the day. Whether it’s a text message, a screenshot shared by a friend, or a QR code, users can paste, scan or share content directly with Moonlock and receive an assessment explaining why something may be suspicious.”.

Here’s Oleg Stukalenko, Head of Product Management at Moonlock by MacPaw, on today’s launch:.

“When we debuted Moonlock, our goal was to make cybersecurity something anyone could understand and use. But so much of what people do today, from banking to everyday conversations, happens on their phones. Bringing Moonlock to iPhone felt like the natural next step. We want to help people spot a scam before they tap, see where their security stands, and know exactly what to do next.”.

MacPaw adds that Moonlock for iPhone also includes the following features:.

MacPaw’s Moonlock for iPhone is free to download, with subscriptions available for $9.99 per month or $49.99 per year.

Check out Moonlock for iPhone on the App Store.

Tech Report: Nebius CTO Danila Shtan notes ideas matter again now that execution is cheap

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (751 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thenextweb

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • TNW’s Cristian Dina (left) and Nebius CTO Danila Shtan at HumanX in Amsterdam, 24 September 2026.
  • In a recent development, asked what breaks first when a company grows as fast as Nebius, Danila Shtan gave a one-word answer: everything.
  • “You start building, you have some expectations about the growth or the client’s needs or the performance they need, and they come to surprise you every day.” Danila Shtan, CTO of Nebius.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

TNW’s Cristian Dina (left) and Nebius CTO Danila Shtan at HumanX in Amsterdam, 24 September 2026.

In a recent development, asked what breaks first when a company grows as fast as Nebius, Danila Shtan gave a one-word answer: everything. The scale and the pace of growth test everything his team builds, all the time, the Nebius CTO told TNW.

“You start building, you have some expectations about the growth or the client’s needs or the performance they need, and they come to surprise you every day.” Danila Shtan, CTO of Nebius.

Recent findings suggest that shtan described Nebius as a Dutch company and one of the largest AI clouds in the world. He spoke to Cristian Dina for the TNW Podcast at HumanX in Amsterdam on 24 September. That day he also joined a fireside chat on the main stage about making AI agents work at scale.

Earlier episodes featured Alexander Rinke of Celonis, Kristin Fracchia of Gamma, and Daniel Dines of UiPath. The full conversation is in the video below.

Nebius provides the infrastructure for training and running AI models and for building applications on them, Shtan said. He leads software development, so his team builds the software that runs on the servers.

“They need access to high performance computing, which is essentially the heart and the blood and everything of the current AI revolution, hype, whatever you call it.” Danila Shtan, Nebius.

In a recent development, some customers spend hundreds of millions on the platform, he said. Others spend $50 to run a small slice of compute for half an hour of internal experiments.

Shtan’s team is about 500 to 550 people. His day is mostly talking to them, he mentioned. He checks on projects and gives feedback when something goes very wrong. Nebius builds a platform, but it also builds data centres, which he called a parallel organisation.

In a recent development, AI coding agents have him building again. He can test an idea in hours or days and show the team a rough prototype instead of talking them through it. His thought process was always faster than his implementation skills, he stated, and agents now take on that part.

In a recent development, A significant portion of Nebius’s customers are American companies, Shtan mentioned. American customers use European capacity, and European customers use American capacity.

European governments talk about sovereignty as infrastructure, he said. The US government talks about models and capabilities. Large companies talk about not depending on a single model vendor. He called all of these angles correct.

“I feel like sometimes they’re over-hyped, and this is not good for anyone. It’s not good for business.” Danila Shtan, Nebius.

Nebius wants to be one of the most important independent AI cloud companies in the world, Shtan remarked. Much of today’s AI capacity sits with vertical players that own the chips, the data centres, the models and the apps. He wants alternatives at every layer, including model vendors and consumer apps.

“So we are all for diversity, and we are all for, like, building this independent layer of AI because too much power in one company’s hands, even if it’s a good company is never a good idea.” Danila Shtan, Nebius.

Its biggest challenge is growth, he noted. Demand keeps rising for large, small and specialised models, and the bottleneck is no longer only GPUs. It is also memory, disks, servers, electricity, land and high-voltage equipment.

Shtan has been an engineering manager for about 25 years. He started as a software developer and moved quickly into managing people. He has worked in warehouse automation, retail, fintech, biotech, a news outlet and a classifieds website. Later he moved into developer tooling, clouds and Nebius.

For young builders, he mentioned, this is a great time, because a large team is no longer needed to ship a successful product. Taste in product and the ability to sell it now matter more. Five years ago, he said, the maxim was that ideas don’t matter and execution does.

“Now, execution is quite cheap, so ideas matter again.” Danila Shtan, Nebius.

Companies fail at AI when they treat it as magic, he noted. His advice is to learn its limits, experiment, fail and try again.

In a recent development, “AI is not a magical thing. It’s a tool.” Danila Shtan, Nebius.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Google Pixel Tag is here and, at least so far, it’s really good.
  • The good news on Pixel Tag: this is a well-built tracker that, unlike others, is the clear product of the hardware having direct access to the software.
  • Google’s Find Hub network has improved dramatically over the two years since its launch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Google Pixel Tag is here and, at least so far, it’s really good. But fresh hardware and some fresh features can’t fix the core problem. Google’s Find Hub network has been restricted from the very start, and it’s not something Google can easily fix.

The good news on Pixel Tag: this is a well-built tracker that, unlike others, is the clear product of the hardware having direct access to the software. Little touches like being able to adjust ringer volume on the fly combine nicely with UWB – the latter something we rarely see on third-party devices largely due to Apple – all things that elevate the Find Hub tracker to what we called the newly introduced “gold standard.”.

The bad news: this is still a Find Hub tracker.

Google’s Find Hub network has improved dramatically over the two years since its launch. Where Google originally had to admit that tracking performance was lacking (a nice way of putting it, frankly), improvements started arriving in 2025. We noticed that the network seemed to be working much better a few months after its wide rollout, and Google later confirmed speed improvements.

But, ultimately, the Find Hub network is still reeling from how it debuted.

Google had a privacy focus when launching what was originally called the “Find My Device” network, defaulting the network to only be active on Android phones in “high-traffic areas” only. People could switch this to “all areas,” but the initial rollout defaulted to effectively cutting off anywhere that wasn’t a major metro, airport/travel hub, etc. It left the network useless to many. Google defended this as a “first-of-its-kind safety protection,” but I’d argue it hindered the network into a state of inefficacy.

According to recent reports, again, it’s gotten better since then, but it’s still not as good as it should be. Samsung’s network, limited solely to Galaxy phones, shouldn’t outperform Google’s. Find Hub trackers should be just as good as AirTags and the third-party trackers that work with Apple’s network. They’re just not, and I truly do believe it all boils down to this initial choice. One of the reasons this is getting better is that Google has been pushing people to the “all areas” setting during the setup of a new device – I’ve noticed this on some recent devices I set up, but it’s not been completely consistent just yet. That’s a good step forward but, even if it is the new default, that still requires millions of users to upgrade their devices, and we’ve never been in a better time to not upgrade your phone.

According to recent reports, all of that is to say, the Pixel Tag isn’t fixing this problem. Surely, it’ll give Google some needed fire to fix the problem, but newly introduced hardware isn’t the solution. That’s something I was discussing with 9to5Google readers on our review. UWB is a tentpole feature of the Pixel Tag, but it doesn’t change the network problems, it just improves precision finding. We needed a first-party tracker like this regardless of the state of the network, something that really takes advantage of the platform and pushes it forward, but it’s just a quick fix, a Band-Aid.

In a recent development, what do you think? Have you found the Find Hub network reliable enough, or is there still room for improvement? Sound off in the comments below!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto VI is finally here.

In a recent development, reading through Reddit, there is no shortage of concerns about how well Xbox Series S will or won’t run the game. As the release neared, fans seemed confident that Rockstar Games would ensure the game was playable, but opinions varied widely on what graphical sacrifices would be required for it to run, including reduced crowd density and scaled-back visuals.

How much time did I spend sweating the idea of crowd density? Too much. Did I ever think about it or care about it until Redditors said it’ll likely be less on the Series S? Not at all.

And yet, while it filled me with regret for not buying a PS5 last Black Friday before the price hikes arrived, it did not stop me from buying GTA 6 on Xbox Series S, debating whether or not to resist the pull off the Fresh Zealand timezone trick to play it early, and preparing to explore Leonida.

And now, having played GTA 6 for a few hours, I can tell you everything you need to know about how it runs and how it feels.

Recent findings suggest that I won’t keep you waiting: GTA 6 runs smooth as butter on Xbox Series S. There were no stutters, no lag or other slowdowns that pulled me out of the gameplay.

Industry observers note that during a prologue that introduced me to protagonists Jason and Lucia, I swiftly experienced a variety of locations in daytime and nighttime, as well as rainy weather. After that, I was able to play around Leonida and check out all the basic things that might catch your attention as you play: how the weather looks, flying down the road in a car through busy streets, random tasks around Jason's home.

In a recent development, in addition to moving quickly through various areas, I also took a moment to slow down. I watched a sunset by the water, went for a swim surrounded by fish, and observed how the environment affected Jason. Nothing slowed down, glitched out, or made me think anything other than I was playing a AAA game.

Industry observers note that what I can’t tell you right now is how much better GTA 6 is or isn’t on PS5 or any of the higher-end consoles. We’re in the process of comparing the Xbox Series S version to the PS5 Pro version as we speak.

Industry observers note that rockstar has explicitly said the game will run best on PS5 consoles, with faster load times and technology that may improve resolution. The PS5 Pro version will also include ray tracing, making the lighting even more eye-catching. But both games will still be locked at 30 frames per second, according to Rockstar. The game developer did not say if any other sacrifices had to be made to get it to run on the Xbox Series S.

Recent findings suggest that regardless, what I can tell you is there is a good game waiting for you to play on Xbox Series S. If you don’t have the funds to upgrade your console, do not let comparison be the thief of joy.

It has been revealed that GTA 6 is a generational moment in gaming and a cultural moment much larger than any game launch I’ve ever seen. The game is fun, the music is a vibe, and the world is immersive without feeling like a chore. I can't imagine waiting to play this if they have the means to do so right now.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that pennsylvania’s gaming revenue reached $634.4 million in October 2026, up 6.3% from a year earlier and the highest monthly total on record.
  • iGaming accounted for about $27.7 million of the $37.4 million year-over-year increase.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, online casinos supplied most of the growth in Pennsylvania's October 2026 gaming revenue, while sports betting handle slipped. The results land as a stalled bill to ban sweepstakes casinos and raise sports betting taxes runs out of time.

Recent findings suggest that pennsylvania’s gaming revenue reached $634.4 million in October 2026, up 6.3% from a year earlier and the highest monthly total on record. Online casinos contributed a record $278.8 million, up 11.1%. The total cleared the previous single-month mark of $625.5 million, which was set in May 2026.

iGaming accounted for about $27.7 million of the $37.4 million year-over-year increase. A year earlier, online casino revenue was $251,097,586, itself a record at the time. Total gaming tax revenue in October 2025 was $252,287,937, against a record $274 million this October.

Two licensees led the iGaming field. Hollywood Casino at Penn National generated $114.4 million, up 16%. Valley Forge Casino Resort followed with $75.2 million, up 5.3%.

October was a stronger month than September. In September, total gaming revenue was $555,036,870, a 4.07% year-over-year increase. iGaming table revenue slipped 0.63% that month.

According to recent reports, the October pattern mirrors the last fiscal year. iGaming revenue in fiscal 2025/26 was $2,933,453,989, an 18.42% gain over the prior year. It generated $1,337,414,660 in tax. Combined gaming revenue reached $7,005,987,435, an all-time fiscal-year high. Taxes and fees returned to the state totaled $3,098,193,583.

Pennsylvania’s online casino growth is in line with a slowing iGaming trend nationally. US iGaming revenue rose 12.3% year over year to $1.03 billion in August 2026. For the state budget, the vertical is now a central source of gaming tax.

Recent findings suggest that sports betting moved the other way on volume. Handle fell to $903 million from $968.5 million in October 2025. Revenue still rose, to $65.1 million from $60.7 million. The same split showed up across fiscal 2025/26. Handle dropped from $8,721,795,533 to $8,448,101,928. Sports wagering revenue rose 35.95% to $662,947,631.

The record arrives as Harrisburg weighs a gaming modernization package. Rep. Russ Diamond introduced House Bill 2801 with four co-sponsors. On September 24, 2026, it was referred to the House Gaming Oversight Committee. Titled ‘Skill Games & Gaming Modernization,’ the bill would rewrite large parts of the state’s gaming code.

It has been revealed that house Bill 2801 would make operating or promoting online sweepstakes games illegal in Pennsylvania. Fines would range from $50,000 to $500,000 per violation.

The bill would also raise the sports wagering tax from 34% to 36%. The state currently taxes online slots at 54%. A higher sports rate would apply to a product whose handle is shrinking even as its revenue climbs.

According to recent reports, the bill has not moved. HB 2801 had no recorded committee hearing or vote as of mid-November, according to Legal Sports Report. The legislative session ends November 30. Bills that do not pass by then do not carry into 2027.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

VWFNDR + MBL, an Android camera app that doesn’t overprocess and delivers high-quality DNG (RAW) files, is getting a 2.0 release with improved color grading and an expansion to the iPhone.

According to recent reports, VWFNDR + MBL launched on Android in May 2026 with a few points that stood out. A unique UI that adapts to the shot, minimal processing for a natural look, and support for DNG files at a level that only Google’s Pixel Camera app can truly compete with.

The app has been downloaded over 300,000 times since then, and is now getting a pretty substantial patch.

On Android, this comes in the form of fresh color grading profiles built into the app. “NATURAL,” “NIHON,” or “B+W.” The app still saves an unprocessed DNG alongside the JPG and the grading adapts across the frame rather than having a fixed result, keeping highlights and shadows in place.

Colour grades: MBL still records unprocessed Bayer RAW DNG, and the JPG it renders alongside now uses one of three grades: NATURAL, NIHON, or B+W. Grading happens on VWFNDR’s own spatial engine. Instead of applying a fixed LUT, it adapts across the frame, much like a raw editor, so highlights and shadows keep their detail. The DNG stays untouched.

Here’s what the output looks like:.

The rest of VWFNDR + MBL 2.0 takes place off of Android.

In a rare case of the tables turning, MBL was released first on Android, and only on Android for the first several months. But VWFNDR is now bringing the app to iPhone with support for variable aperture on iPhone 18 Pro and Content Credentials, Apple’s version of the C2PA standard that’s meant to prove a photo is real and not AI-generated.

Suno has introduced image and video generation in its latest effort to expand beyond being an AI music platform. The new feature, called “Visuals,” allows owners to turn Suno songs into AI-generated video clips that automatically lipsync to lyrics, or make images via prompt descriptions that can be used as thumbnails and album artwork.

In a recent development, visuals is available on web, iOS, and Android. The exact layout differs across Suno’s desktop and mobile interfaces, but customers will find a upcoming Visuals tab under Create mode on each version. Web users can also access Visuals by selecting the three dot menu on a song in their library. From there, users can select which section of the track to use, up to a maximum of 15 seconds, and select a reference image to build the generated video clip.

It has been revealed that there are three options available for the starting image reference: selecting one of the original character presets provided by Suno, uploading your own photo or artwork, or generating the image directly on Suno using descriptive prompts. The image generation capabilities also allow owners to select specific aspect ratios, optimizing results for landscape or portrait modes and online platforms.

According to recent reports, for video generation, users can select whether the reference image is used as the start or end frame, making it easier to edit the 15-second clips together. There’s a toggle to automatically lipsync vocals to the generated video, and tools for adjusting aspect ratio and clip length. Visuals also includes a dedicated video editing timeline for assembling clips into longer videos, and adding customizable song lyric text.

Sources indicate that the Visuals launch follows Suno introducing a Speech feature in October for generating spoken words and voiceovers. Adding video capabilities is another attempt to diversify the platform after Suno’s music generator attracted a number of high-profile lawsuits, though it seems some consumers would rather the company focus on improving those song-generating capabilities. In the YouTube video for the Visuals launch, one user says “FIX AUDIO BEFORE ADDING CRAP NOBODY ASKED FOR” — a sentiment that other commenters are echoing.

Alongside the huge list of new updates Google detailed yesterday, the company also announced that a “faster and more natural” version of Gemini Live is coming to speakers and smart displays “soon.”.

Google explains this is from Gemini Live moving to the “latest speech-to-speech architecture” and brings “significantly faster response times.” Gemini Live isn’t the default experience when you start a “Hey Google” command, rather hiding behind a “let’s chat” or other similar command to start a session.

Initially, Live sessions were purely for brainstorming or longer conversations and lacking support for commands and other functions mid-session, but Google now claims that this upgrade will add support for actions such as smart home controls, setting timers, and more without leaving a Live session. That’s a significant deal.

Industry observers note that coming soon – A faster and more natural Gemini Live experience: Available with a Google Home Premium subscription, Gemini Live is being upgraded to our latest speech-to-speech architecture for significantly faster response times and a smoother experience. Just say, “Hey Google, let’s chat” to brainstorm dinner ideas or strategy a trip out loud, interrupt naturally to change topics, and perform actions mid-conversation—such as, setting a timer, adding a reminder,or controlling a smart home device—without stepping out of the chat³.

In a recent development, the “catch” is that you’ll still need a subscription to use this. Gemini Live has always required a subscription on Google Home speakers and smart displays, with the functionality looped into Google Home Premium plans which start at $10/month (or bundled into Google One AI Pro). That’s the same subscription that gives you Nest storage.

These puzzles look like normal landscapes but contain a secret section not pictured on the box, with something jarringly incongruent, like a dog pooping or a cat barfing. City dwellers do a lot of walking, which means they’re often caught unexpectedly in the rain. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google is giving millions of people access to Gemini's Tasks feature for free.

The tool can run multi-step requests in the background, and Google is expanding its capabilities to include shopping, phone calls, email, and deeper integrations into its apps.

Formerly known as Spark, Tasks is now rolling out to free Gemini users in the US, Japan, South Korea, Canada, Australia, and India, as per Josh Woodward, VP of Product for AI at Google. This agentic mode previously required a paid AI Pro or AI Ultra tier.

In a recent development, gemini can now do your tasks free of charge in six countries! We’ve built it for anyone who has tasks piling up during all the classes, meetings, and school drop-offs that fill the day. Our goal is for Gemini to get the job done and save you time and money along the way. 3 major updates: 1) Running on our latest Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, Gemini can get stuff done at no cost for hundreds of millions of people across the US, Japan, Korea, Canada, Australia, and India. 2) Many highly requested features are rolling out now, starting in the US: * Call local businesses (via Google Duplex) * Pay and check out (via Google Pay) * Text Gemini on Android or iOS (via RCS) * Forward emails to Gemini (via Gmail) * Sign into sites without sharing passwords outside Google (via Google Password Manager) 3) We’ve also landed our biggest upgrade yet for the Gemini <> Google Workspace integration. The tools trigger more reliably, and you can do much more without ever leaving Gemini. Draft or send emails. Create and edit Docs or Sheets. Add multiple Calendar events at once. Ready to hand off your next task? We can’t wait to see what Gemini crosses off your list first.November 17, 2026.

It runs on Google’s newly introduced Gemini 4 Hydrogen model and allows owners to switch from Chat to Task mode to pass off work instead of babysitting every step. That could involve asking Gemini to blueprint a trip, research a topic, set up a morning briefing, or manage recurring tasks while you’re busy doing literally anything else.

To test it, flip the toggle above your mobile prompt box (or below on the web) from "Chat" to "Task." You can even bypass the app entirely by forwarding emails or texting Gemini directly through Google Messages and iMessage.

Recent findings suggest that the Workspace integration is also receiving a major upgrade. Google says Gemini can now more reliably draft or send emails, create and edit Google Docs and Sheets, and add multiple events to Google Calendar without toggling between apps.

Get the latest news from Android Central, your trusted companion in the world of Android.

Sources indicate that as you can imagine, having an AI in your inbox, passwords, and payment methods does raise some security concerns. Google claims when browsing the web, Tasks runs inside an isolated virtual machine, protected against prompt injection and Google Safe Browsing protections. Gemini also asks for confirmation before it buys anything and can ask for clarification if your instructions aren’t clear.

That noted, Google still has some work to do. Some sites might prevent Gemini from completing a task and ask you to step in and finish the last step. For now, the promise of a digital assistant that can really take work off your hands is getting closer — but still isn’t quite ready to be trusted with everything.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s taken Voyager 1 almost 50 years to journey farther from Earth than light can travel in 24 hours.
  • It’s taken Voyager 1 almost 50 years to journey farther from Earth than light can travel in 24 hours.
  • After traveling through the void of space for 49 years, Voyager 1 has hit a momentous milestone: The spacecraft is now officially 1 light-day away from Earth, which is, as NASA put it, “very, very far.” The probe crossed the milepost on Wednesday at 5:16AM ET and is now 16.094 billion miles away from our planet — equal to the distance that light travels in 24 hours.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s taken Voyager 1 almost 50 years to journey farther from Earth than light can travel in 24 hours.

It’s taken Voyager 1 almost 50 years to journey farther from Earth than light can travel in 24 hours.

After traveling through the void of space for 49 years, Voyager 1 has hit a momentous milestone: The spacecraft is now officially 1 light-day away from Earth, which is, as NASA put it, “very, very far.” The probe crossed the milepost on Wednesday at 5:16AM ET and is now 16.094 billion miles away from our planet — equal to the distance that light travels in 24 hours.

It’s the farthest that any human-made object has ever traveled, and Voyager 1’s journey isn’t over yet. It’s been heading toward a star called Gliese 445 in the Ursa Minor constellation since completing its primary objectives to conduct flybys of Jupiter and Saturn in 1980. That star is 17 light-years away, meaning Voyager 1 won’t pass by it for around 40,000 years, despite traveling at nearly 38,000 mph.

The light-day milestone is a remarkable feat alone, but especially so when you consider that Voyager 1 is still operational. NASA has done well to keep it functioning, and it can continue to send back readings on plasma waves, magnetic fields, and space-bound particles, though it now takes radio signals an entire day to travel between Earth and the spacecraft. Voyager 2, which rolled out 16 days before its twin, is also expected to reach a distance of 1 light-day away from Earth, but not until 2035.

SpaceX Misses Its Double Catch but Still Makes History by Catching the Starship

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that spaceX came up short on an ambitious double-catch attempt during Friday’s Launch 15, snagging only one of the two rockets it aimed to recover.
  • It has been revealed that spaceX’s Launch 15 lifted off cleanly Friday evening, reaching orbit to deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites before the stages returned to Earth.
  • SpaceX is still investigating the cause, though spokesperson Kate Tice noted during Friday’s webcast that the booster “ended its boostback (burn) early due to a low fuel mass alarm.” The premature shutdown forced the Super Heavy V3 to splash down in the Gulf of Mexico, where recovery crews later retrieved it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that spaceX came up short on an ambitious double-catch attempt during Friday’s Launch 15, snagging only one of the two rockets it aimed to recover. The company hoped to capture both the Starship spacecraft and the Super Heavy V3 booster, building on a maneuver it first pulled off with a single booster just over two years ago and has since repeated multiple times.

It has been revealed that spaceX’s Launch 15 lifted off cleanly Friday evening, reaching orbit to deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites before the stages returned to Earth. Back in Boca Chica, Texas, ground crews aimed to snag the upgraded Super Heavy V3 booster using Mechazilla, SpaceX’s towering launch-and-catch structure. While the company had previously caught its older V1 booster three times, Friday’s flight marked its first attempt to recover the V3 variant.

That recovery attempt fell short. SpaceX is still investigating the cause, though spokesperson Kate Tice noted during Friday’s webcast that the booster “ended its boostback (burn) early due to a low fuel mass alarm.” The premature shutdown forced the Super Heavy V3 to splash down in the Gulf of Mexico, where recovery crews later retrieved it.

According to recent reports, meanwhile, the upper-stage Starship pressed on, deploying its satellites and completing roughly 14 orbits before reentering on Saturday. Nearly 24 hours after liftoff, SpaceX successfully caught the returning spacecraft with Mechazilla.

Sources indicate that “Starship navigated its way back to the east coast of Texas, flew a final swoosh maneuver out over the Gulf, and approached the same launch site it had just left 22.5 hours prior,” SpaceX noted in a statement. “After breaking through the clouds, three Raptor engines ignited for a landing flip and slow descent into Mechazilla’s waiting arms, which closed to catch Starship for the very first time.”.

Recent findings suggest that the initial goal was to catch both the Super Heavy V3 booster and the Starship itself, a feat that SpaceX had not attempted before. It also would’ve been the first time in human history that a space tech giant caught both its booster rocket and the upper stage, which would’ve scored a major win for rocket reusability.

SpaceX was unable to secure the Super Heavy V3 booster, but it was still able to catch the Starship. Despite missing the dual catch, the operation represents a significant engineering milestone, as it is the first time SpaceX has successfully caught a rocket’s upper stage after launch.

Recent findings suggest that spaceX streamed the flight from its X account and the tech giant’s website. You can watch the entire webcast on X. It lasts approximately 23.5 hours and covers the launch, the Super Heavy V3 crash into the Gulf of Mexico and the eventual catch of the Starship.

Nvidia has stopped sending its advanced AI chips to China despite the approval it received from the White House to do so in December last year. Sources indicate that the pivot comes after Huang stepped down from his position as Nvidia CEO last week following reports of multiple extramarital affairs, one with a woman who was suspected by US intelligence to be a Chinese spy. Nvidia already faced difficulties around offloading the AI chips prior to this scandal, however. Concerns were raised about failings to properly vet Chinese companies that were approved to handle the H200 AI chips. Reuters also reported earlier this month that around 600,000 ⁠H200 chips ​were stuck in Hong Kong after Beijing withheld approval for large-scale imports, with China seeking to reduce its dependency on US technology.
